MedPlus Health Services
sells standard home healthcare and monitoring devices (such as blood pressure monitors, digital thermometers, and weighing scales), but
it does not actively sell or distribute high-tech wearable medical devices
(like continuous glucose monitors, medical alert smartwatches, or clinical ECG wearables) through its retail or online pharmacy platform (
MedPlusMart
MedPlusMart
Product Offerings
Home Healthcare Devices:
Blood pressure monitors, nebulizers, digital thermometers, and weighing scales.
Wellness & OTC Items:
Basic first-aid, surgical consumables, and nutritional supplements.
Exclusions:
Consumer fitness trackers or clinical-grade wearable health sensors are generally absent from their active inventory.

The out-of-pocket cost of a Continuous Glucose Monitor (CGM) generally ranges from
$50 to $400 per month
($600 to $4,800 per year) without insurance
. If covered by commercial insurance or Medicare, the cost typically drops to
$20 or less per month
Healthline
The total financial commitment depends heavily on whether you use a prescription medical model or a newer over-the-counter (OTC) model.

No prescription needed. Best for people with prediabetes, type 2 diabetes not using insulin, or health enthusiasts. Bypasses insurance.
Mid-Tier Prescription
Abbott FreeStyle Libre 3 Plus
$130 – $160
Prescription required. Lower cash price for traditional CGMs. Sensors last 14 to 15 days. Often requires manufacturer coupons to get the lowest price.
Premium Prescription
Dexcom G7
$250 – $400
Prescription required. Highly accurate, integrates with insulin pumps, and includes advanced low-sugar alarms. Sensors last 10 days.
Additional Costs to Consider
Hardware Requirements
: Most modern CGMs send data directly to a free smartphone app. However, if you do not have a compatible smartphone, standalone receiver devices can cost a one-time fee of
$100 to $450
GoodRx
Subscription Programs
: Wellness platforms like
Nutrisense
bundle CGMs with dietitian coaching, which usually prices out at
$180 to $300+ per month
GoodRx
Ways to Lower the Cost
Manufacturer Savings Cards
: Companies like Abbott and Dexcom offer pharmacy vouchers that can lower out-of-pocket costs to around $75 a month, even if your insurance denies the claim.
YouTube
Hack Your Blood Sugar
Shop Around
: Retail pharmacy prices vary significantly. Using coupon services like
GoodRx
can highlight which local pharmacy has the lowest base retail price.
Check OTC Eligibility
: If you do not require urgent, real-time insulin pump integration, opt for an OTC brand like Stelo to bypass expensive clinical markups.
